claim: ADR 0281 F2 (founder, 2026-10-05: "Re-date all, keep undo (Recommended)"): migration old_pos_rows_carry_their_check_date re-dates the POS rows written before #603 to LEAST(pos_checks.closed_at, created_at), exactly the rows the read-only dry run calls change, and logs every old date first so it can be undone. Read statically from the migration with -- comments stripped and whitespace collapsed: one file carries the slug; public.pos_row_redate_undo keeps old_transaction_date, old_recorded_at, old_created_at and new_date, has RLS on, and is revoked from PUBLIC, anon, authenticated and service_role, as are the three functions (none SECURITY DEFINER); the classification targets LEAST(c.closed_at, m.entry), keeps the dry run's outcome order (out of scope, ambiguous, no check, check open, unreadable, already, change) and links a glass-pour row through its pos: pour event at the same created_at; the write logs and updates only change rows, sets inventory_transactions.transaction_date and nothing else on the ledger, sets wine_consumption_log.recorded_at and created_at together, and touches no other table (no UPDATE, INSERT or DELETE on pos_checks or pour_events, no TRUNCATE, no DISABLE TRIGGER); the undo restores a row only while it still carries the run's new date and goes newest run first; the migration halts before writing if pg_trigger or pg_rules shows anything on either table; and it calls the write once. What this does not check: that the SQL behaves as written (the SQL test of the same slug does, on local Postgres; CI does not run supabase/tests), and production's triggers (not read). Measured 2026-10-05: exit 0 on this branch; exit 1 on origin/main e1d65b3ad (no such migration). Mutated in a scratch copy (PR body): each property above, broken alone, exits 1.
